tools.name: camera_status
tools.description:
Reports the camera connection, its USB mode, and which features work in that mode.

Best for: the first call in any camera task, and after any needs_* error.
Returns: link, reason, model, firmware, mode, capture (stills/movie), screen, battery, card, keep_awake (the setting) and keep_awake_active (resetting the camera's auto power off timer now), the owner process (serve, its pid, fake or real camera), and available per feature (settings, slots, movie_props).
Not for property values: use settings_read.

tools.name: camera_watch
tools.description:
Returns the change groups the camera reported after a cursor, waiting up to wait_s for new ones.

Best for: Lab mapping (ask the user to turn a dial, then call this), and checking a change the user made on the camera body.
Returns: { cursor, link, groups: [{ id, at, source: camera|write, changes: [{ code, name, old, new, old_label, new_label }] }], has_more }. Without since, only groups that arrive during the call. Pass the returned cursor as since on the next call so nothing is missed.
Query tips: codes filters the groups to those codes; it does not change what the camera polls.
Follow up with catalog_label to name a code that moved.

since.description: The cursor from the last camera_watch: return groups after it.

wait_s.description: How long to wait for a group when none is there yet.

tools.name: settings_read
tools.description:
Reads live camera settings with their catalog names, menu paths and value labels.

Best for: "what is X set to", finding a setting by name or menu, browsing the menu tree.
Returns: { rows: [{ code, name, menu, value, value_label, options?, writable, confidence, available, error? }], total, has_more }. options (the allowed values) appear when 10 rows or fewer match. view=menus returns { menus: [{ path, depth, count }] } instead.
Query tips: query words must all appear in the code, the name (FaceEyeDetection matches "eye detection"), the menu path or the notes. menu is a path prefix: "SET UP > POWER MANAGEMENT". Needs USB TETHER mode, except with codes, which read in any connected mode.
Follow up with camera_plan to change a value. Owner strings (copyright, author) are settings too: query "copyright".

filter.description: unnamed: codes with no catalog name. unconfirmed: codes whose catalog confidence is not confirmed.

tools.name: camera_plan
tools.description:
Builds a change plan against the live camera. Writes nothing.

Best for: every camera write: one setting, several, or owner strings.
Returns: { plan_id, expires_in_s, requires, steps: [{ code, name, menu, before, after, confidence, gate }], skipped: [{ code, name, value, reason, message }], blocked: [...], allow_unconfirmed }. blocked steps are not written; skipped ones need nothing (unchanged) or another mode.
Query tips: set maps a name to a value. The name is a catalog name (AutoPowerOff), a menu label ("AUTO POWER OFF") or a code (0xd381); the value is a value label (OFF) or a raw number. An unknown or ambiguous name or value fails with the valid choices.
A plan with nothing to write fails with the reason (unconfirmed_property, needs_tether ...). allow_unconfirmed lets the plan write codes whose catalog confidence is not confirmed: only when the user asks.
Follow up with camera_apply and the plan_id, after the user agrees to the steps.

tools.name: camera_apply
tools.description:
Applies a plan made by camera_plan: writes each step to the camera, reads it back, and logs it.

Best for: the second step of every camera write, after the user agreed to the plan's steps.
Returns: { plan_id, applied, failed, not_attempted, undo_plan_id, steps: [{ code, name, wanted, readback, ok, result, error, attempts }], side_effects }. A plan applies once.
Refuses with plan_stale when a planned code changed since the plan, and plan_expired after 5 minutes or a restart of the owner: make a new plan. Stops at the first failed step; apply undo_plan_id to revert what was written.

tools.name: catalog_label
tools.description:
Edits one property's entry in the connected model's catalog: name, menu path, value labels, confidence, notes. Never writes to the camera.

Best for: Lab mapping, after camera_watch showed a code move.
Returns: { model, path, code, entry }.
Query tips: an empty string clears a field; an empty label removes that value. confidence confirmed needs this session to have seen the code change (on the camera, or a write's read-back), else no_evidence. Text that matches a string the camera reports (serials, owner strings) is refused with private_text: the catalog is shared.
Not for camera values: use camera_plan.

menu.description: The menu path: SET UP > POWER MANAGEMENT > AUTO POWER OFF.

tools.name: fake_camera
tools.description:
Drives the fake camera, as the person at the camera would. Only with UKIYO_FAKE_CAMERA=1.

Best for: testing a flow without hardware: open a menu, flip STILL/MOVIE, power off, unplug, nudge a random setting, start or stop automatic changes.
Returns: { action }.
